# Requirements

---
## Table of contents
[Recipe](#recipe)\
[Ingredients](#ingredients)\
[Shopping List](#shopping-list)\
[Goods](#goods)

---
### Recipe

A Recipe needs to contain information about the ingredients for the recipe but also instructions on how to process the ingredients.
The user shall be able to create recipes inside this app and store them together with the ingredients of the specific recipe.
Also, it shall be possible to add a recipe to the shopping-list instead of a single ingredient. Along with that, it would be nice if the 
 number of people that this recipe is meant for can be edited when adding the recipe to the shopping-list.
All recipes shall be stored in a database. There needs to be a possibility to create new recipes and refactor the existing recipes.

---
### Ingredients

An Ingredient has an ID that is exclusive for the ingredient and a string representing the name of the ingredient, which also needs to be exclusive.
The ingredients shall be stored in a database. There needs to be the possibility to add new ingredients and refactor ingredients.

---
### Shopping List

A shopping list contains Ingredients that are to be bought. The ingredients need to be removable from the list.
It shall be possible to add all ingredients of a recipe with a default amount. 
The amount of ingredients shall be adjustable by giving the recipe a number of people that this recipe is meant for. 

---
### Goods

Goods are non-edible things that can be added to the shopping list. 
They need to have an id that is exclusive for the good and also a string representing the name of the good, which also needs to be exclusive.

Good start. The hollow diamonds imply “has-a” without lifecycle ownership. For a shopping list/recipe domain, you usually want explicit entry objects and composition to model ownership of those entries.

### Suggested tweaks
- Use composition for owned entries:
 - `ShoppingList` owns `ShoppingListItem`
 - `Recipe` owns `RecipeIngredient`
- Keep ingredients/non-food as reusable catalog items (no ownership by a specific list/recipe).
- Unify `Ingredient` and `NonFoodItem` under a common `AbstractItem` (or `Product/Item`) if you want shared behavior.
- Add multiplicities and move “quantity/unit/notes” onto the entry classes.

```plantuml
@startuml
hide empty members

abstract class AbstractItem
class Ingredient
class NonFoodItem
Ingredient --|> AbstractItem
NonFoodItem --|> AbstractItem

class ShoppingList
class ShoppingListItem {
 quantity
 unit
 notes
}

class Recipe
class RecipeIngredient {
 quantity
 unit
}

ShoppingList "1" *-- "0..*" ShoppingListItem
ShoppingListItem --> "1" AbstractItem

Recipe "1" *-- "1..*" RecipeIngredient
RecipeIngredient --> "1" Ingredient

' Optional: a list can also reference planned recipes (not ownership)
ShoppingList --> "0..*" Recipe : planned
@enduml
```

- Use filled diamond `*--` where the parent controls lifecycle (entries).
- Use plain association `-->` from entries to items (catalog entities live independently).

- If you keep your current structure, change `o--` to simple associations or move to the composition pattern above to avoid implying the list “owns” `AbstractIngredient/AbstractNonFoodItem`.

- You could also rename `AbstractNonFoodItem` to `AbstractGeneralMerchandise` or just `NonFoodItem`.

- Multiplicities will make the intent clear to readers.

- In short: model entries as owned parts; items/ingredients remain reusable.

In that draft, only the concrete classes realized the interfaces, and nothing else depended on those interfaces. To make the interfaces “used,” either:
- Have the abstract base realize the interface, and/or
- Add a client that depends on the interfaces (ports), or
- Point associations at the interface instead of the concrete/abstract class where appropriate.

### Minimal tweak that shows real interface usage
```plantuml
@startuml
hide empty members

' Catalog
abstract class Item
class Ingredient
class NonFoodItem
Ingredient --|> Item
NonFoodItem --|> Item

' Recipe
interface RecipeInterface
abstract class AbstractRecipe
class RecipeIngredient
class ConcreteRecipe

AbstractRecipe ..|> RecipeInterface
ConcreteRecipe --|> AbstractRecipe
AbstractRecipe "1" *-- "1..*" RecipeIngredient
RecipeIngredient --> "1" Ingredient

' Shopping list
interface ShoppingListInterface
abstract class AbstractShoppingList
class ShoppingListItem
class ConcreteShoppingList

AbstractShoppingList ..|> ShoppingListInterface
ConcreteShoppingList --|> AbstractShoppingList
AbstractShoppingList "1" *-- "0..*" ShoppingListItem
ShoppingListItem --> "1" Item

' A client depending on interfaces (ports)
class Planner
Planner ..> RecipeInterface
Planner ..> ShoppingListInterface
@enduml
```

- Interfaces are realized by the abstract bases.
- A client (`Planner`) depends on the interfaces, not on concrete classes.
- Domain parts (`RecipeIngredient`, `ShoppingListItem`, `Item`) stay decoupled from service interfaces.
